The '''1998–99''' season was '''Chelsea F.C.'s''' 85th competitive season, seventh consecutive season in the [[Premier League]] and 93rd year as a club.

==Season summary==
After a solid fourth-place finish coupled with European and [[League Cup]] success the previous season, Chelsea really felt that they could challenge for the title this season. Chelsea made more big name signings, including [[France national football team|French]] [[FIFA World Cup|World Cup]] winning defender [[Marcel Desailly]] from [[A.C. Milan]], [[Spain national football team|Spanish]] international full-back [[Albert Ferrer]] from [[F.C. Barcelona|Barcelona]] and, in a club-record £5.4 million move, [[Italy national football team|Italian]] international striker [[Pierluigi Casiraghi]] from [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]]. Casiraghi's season and career was cut short by a knee injury, but his compatriot [[Gianfranco Zola]] had arguably the best season of his career, leading Chelsea to a serious title challenge, scoring 15 goals in all competitions and setting up many other goals for his teammates.

Ultimately, the [[European Super Cup]], won by beating Champions League winners [[Real Madrid C.F.|Real Madrid]], was the only trophy that Chelsea had to show for them. Their defence of the now-defunct [[European Cup Winners' Cup|Cup Winners' Cup]] ended in the semi-finals, while their title challenge was ended in early May when they couldn't get the better of [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] or [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]. Nonetheless, a final third-place finish booked them their first ever [[UEFA Champions League]] campaign and was another triumph for their young manager [[Gianluca Vialli]], who, at 35, announced his retirement as a player to concentrate on his managerial duties.
